gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker 12-in-1 strip (A91F4), which ChatGPT listed at 'up to 35W', delivers 35 W only when USB-C1 is the only port in use and drops to 20 W + 15 W when all four ports are used, or that it is rated 900 J, while the Anker 351 ($28.99) and TESSAN PS07 ($28.99) are rated 2,100 J and cost less.
standout_why: Six rival pages compared. rottenwifi.com says the Anker 351's USB-C reaches 20 W only when both USB-A ports are idle, so that point is covered. laptopbee.com, inspectandtest.net, itechguides.com and geekchamp.com only say in general terms that USB output is shared. None of those five mentions the A91F4 or the Nano 67W (A9129), so none has their per-combination wattage or the A91F4's 900 J rating. anker.com's blog gives single-port maximums only. Tom's Guide (the cited page) returned a 121-character stub through WebFetch, and the curl attempt was not approved, so it is unchecked.
decides: This supports the Anker 351 / TESSAN PS07 tier (both $28.99, 2,100 J) for a typical desk. ChatGPT's 'more USB-C ports' pick, the A91F4, costs $1 more, has under half the surge rating and charges at 20 W once a second device is plugged in, the same as the 351. Only the charging-station class (Nano 67W, Prime 140W, TESSAN 65W hub) gives more than 20 W with several devices plugged in. Those have only 2 or 3 AC outlets, and Anker gives no joule rating for the 67 W model and says the 140 W model has no surge protection. Both Anker stations are sold out on anker.com today.
